message:
Wait, I need to reconsider step 11. Let me re-examine the vulnerable code more carefully.

Looking at the fix commit:
```c
-       if ((caps = memchr(line, '\0', len)) != NULL) {
+       if ((caps = memchr(line, '\0', len)) != NULL &&
+           len > (size_t)((caps - line) + 1)) {
                caps++;
```

The fix checks `len > (size_t)((caps - line) + 1)`. This means the vulnerable condition is when `len <= (caps - line) + 1`, i.e., when `caps - line >= len - 1`, i.e., when the null byte is at position `len - 1` or beyond (but `memchr` only searches within `len` bytes, so the null byte can be at most at position `len - 1`).

So the null byte is at position `len - 1 = 65530` (0-indexed from `line`). Then `caps = line + 65530 + 1 = line + 65531 = buf->data + 4 + 65531 = buf->data + 65535`.

Then `caps++` makes `caps = buf->data + 65536`, which is one past the end of the buffer.

Then `strncmp(caps, "object-format=", 14)` reads from `buf->data + 65536`, which is a heap-buffer-overflow READ.

So my trace is correct. Let me verify the trace file was created:

</｜｜DSML｜｜>
